character_sheet: A low, creeping insect horror: a body block with five 'insides' pieces at its centre, four two-part legs splayed out to the sides, two two-part pincers at the front, a three-segment tail curling up behind and five spikes on its back (ModelCreepingHorror.java:48-73; 26 parts on a 128x128 sheet). It is hostile but weak: 10 HP, 3 damage, 2 armour, speed 0.25 (MobStats.CREEPING_HORROR, CreepingHorror.java:85-93). Every fifth tick it hunts anything alive and in sight within 16 blocks - its own kind, the mod's scenery and ally mobs and creative players excepted (:145-200) - walks at it at 1.25 and bites within 2.2 blocks on 1-in-12-or-1-in-14 dice (:153-163, doHurtTarget :159); it retaliates when hit (:82), floats (:69), panics (:70), walks through villages (:78) and strolls avoiding water (:79). It spawns in darkness at night in the Chaos dimension or below y 15 (:100-112) and tends to vanish by day (:114-123). Read it as a skittering bug: legs sweeping wide with the stride, pincers working, the tail pumping up and down, the five spikes quivering on fifteen different beats.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.75 of the rig (CreepingHorrorRenderer.java:25, 38) on a 128x128 sheet (ModelCreepingHorror.java:184); the hitbox is 0.75 x 0.5 (ModEntities.java:73-75); shadow 0.45 x 0.75 (CreepingHorrorRenderer.java:27).

labels.leg1part2: left front leg, lower (moves with the upper)

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: rests +0.576 rad (left front, right back) and -0.576 (left back, right front), then pi x 0.35 = 1.1 rad (63 deg) x the walking speed at 1.25, no threshold
groups.plain: the four legs sweep wide fore and aft with the stride, upper and lower parts together: the left front and right back one way, the other two the opposite
groups.math: a = cos(ageInTicks * 1.25) * pi * 0.35 * limbSwingAmount; leg1/leg1part2.yRot = 0.576 + a; leg2/leg2part2.yRot = -0.576 - a; leg3/leg3part2.yRot = -0.576 - a; leg4/leg4part2.yRot = 0.576 + a
groups.omega_note: the phase is ageInTicks x 1.25 (no wingspeed): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.25 = 5 ticks

groups.name: pincers
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg), the left pincer the mirror of the right, no rest offset
groups.plain: the two pincers open and close together at all times
groups.math: p = cos(ageInTicks * 0.48) * pi * 0.15; pincer1/pincer1part2.yRot = p; pincer2/pincer2part2.yRot = -p
groups.omega_note: the phase is ageInTicks x 0.48: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.48 = 13.1 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: rests -0.55 / 0 / -0.22 rad (base, middle, tip), then pi x 0.25 = 0.785 rad (45 deg), rectified (|cos|: the tail pumps up and drops twice per natural period), the same angle on all three segments
groups.plain: the tail pumps up from its curl and settles, slowly, all three segments together
groups.math: n = abs(cos(ageInTicks * 0.11) * pi * 0.25); tailseg1.xRot = -0.55 + n; tailseg2.xRot = n; tailseg3.xRot = -0.22 + n
groups.omega_note: the phase is ageInTicks x 0.11: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.11 = 57.1 ticks, the visible pump every 28.6

groups.name: spikes
groups.axis: x, y and z - each spike on three rates of its own
groups.amplitude: pitch: 0.7 rad rest then pi x 0.08 = 0.251 rad (14 deg); yaw and roll: pi x 0.08 around 0 - fifteen cosines, one per spike per axis
groups.plain: the five back spikes quiver, each on its own three beats, never in step
groups.omega_note: fifteen rates in one group: the omega here is spike1's pitch, 0.81 (period 7.8 ticks); spikes 4 and 5 pitch at 0.103 and 0.107 (periods 61 and 59 ticks - ten times slower than the first three, a likely slip in the 1.7.10 constants kept as-is); author one quiver at 0.81 and offset the other spikes and axes

behaviour: One gait rhythm on the legs (ModelCreepingHorror.java:189-193): the cosine of the age x 1.25, x pi x 0.35, x the walking speed (63 degrees at full speed every 5 ticks, no threshold) is added to the +0.576 rad rests of the left front and right back legs and subtracted from the -0.576 rests of the other two, the lower part of each leg copying the upper - a wide sideways sweep; at a standstill the legs sit on their rests.
The pincers open and close at all times (:194-197): the cosine of the age x 0.48, x pi x 0.15 - 27 degrees every 13.1 ticks - on the right pincer's two pieces, and its negative on the left.

The tail pumps (:198-202): the absolute value of the cosine of the age x 0.11 x pi x 0.25 (45 degrees, rectified - a rise and fall every 28.6 ticks) is added to the base's -0.55 rad, the middle's 0 and the tip's -0.22, all three segments turning by the same angle.

The five spikes quiver on fifteen beats (:203-222): each pitches 14 degrees around 0.7 rad at 0.81, 0.87, 0.99, 0.103 and 0.107, yaws 14 degrees at 1.11 to 1.31 and rolls 14 degrees at 1.41 to 1.61 - spikes 4 and 5 pitch ten times slower than the first three (0.103 and 0.107 read like 1.03 and 1.07 mistyped in the original; kept).

The body and the five insides pieces never move; nothing reads the look (netHeadYaw unused), so the LookAtPlayerGoal (CreepingHorror.java:80) turns nothing visible. There is no attacking flag: the bite (doHurtTarget :159, within 2.2 blocks on dice) has no pose of its own.

clips.note: ruled 2026-09-06, Q3 (a): the vanilla death flip stays; a creature whose JSON ships a `death` clip gets the clip-replaces-flip mode, designed when the first such clip arrives (the Queen's own death clip the precedent) - a `death` delivered here plays under the flip until then

wishlist: in `walk`: bend the legs - the lower part copies the upper (ModelCreepingHorror.java:190-193), so each leg is a rigid V; a lift of the lower part as the leg swings forward makes a skitter
the fifteen spike beats (:203-222) cannot survive one phase-locked loop: quiver the spikes at one rate with five phase offsets and vary the amplitude a little per spike
in `attack`: a lunge - the bite (CreepingHorror.java:159) has no pose today; close both pincers on the impact frame and pump the tail up
in `idle`: a breath in the body block and a shift of the insides pieces (they never move) so the horror reads as something alive under the shell
in `hurt`: a scuttle back with the tail thrown high
